cards.explanation: The answer is that they stumbled because of their sin. The call says, "…for you have stumbled by your iniquity." Stumbled, like a toe catching the edge of the rug. I've tripped over my own mustache more times than I can count, friends, so I know that feeling. And the way back is named in the very same breath: "Return, O Israel, to the LORD your God…"

The answer is confessions. The verse says, "Bring your confessions and return to the LORD." Confessions are the very thing it names. I think that's a comfort for anybody who ever walked into a room with empty pockets.

The answer is all of it! The words say, "Take away all our iniquity…" Not a piece of it, not the easy part. I love that the words they're given hand the whole pile over. When you're sweeping up a mess, the broom works best when you stop hiding crumbs under the rug.

The answer is Assyria. In the words Israel is given, they say, "Assyria will not save us, nor will we ride on horses." Assyria is the name those words pick. I think that's a big thing to say out loud, friends.
The answer is True. The words say, "We will never again say, ‘Our gods!’ to the work of our own hands." Israel is given those words to say. I think that takes courage.

The answer is the fatherless. The words end with, "For in You the fatherless find compassion." That's the line they close on. I know a little about being left in the dark and then found, so this line lands with me.

The answer is that He'll heal it! The LORD says, "I will heal their apostasy…" Apostasy is turning away from Him. His answer is healing. Friends, I'd have taken a long pause here too, because that's some good news.

The answer is False, and I'm so glad. The LORD says, "I will freely love them, for My anger has turned away from them." Freely, friends, with no earning. I like a cookie cooling on the rack, and no one has to pay admission to love it.
The answer is anger. The LORD says, "I will freely love them, for My anger has turned away from them." That's the reason He gives. I'm over a burnt batch in about ten minutes, so I admire this.

The answer is dew! The LORD says, "I will be like the dew to Israel…" I think dew is a gentle picture, though that's my own thought. The verse just says dew and then goes straight to blossoming. A picture like that makes me want to open the bakery window.
The answer is False. The LORD says Israel "…will blossom like the lily and take root like the cedars of Lebanon." Blossoming on top and roots underneath. Nobody in this picture is wilting in the sun.
The answer is grain! The verse says, "They will return and dwell in his shade; they will grow grain and blossom like the vine." It's a picture of growth. Friends, that's a lot of good in one verse.

The answer is True. The LORD says, "O Ephraim, what have I to do anymore with idols? It is I who answer and watch over him." He speaks to Ephraim here. He says He is the One who answers and watches over him.

The answer is from the LORD Himself. The LORD says, "I am like a flourishing cypress; your fruit comes from Me." Ephraim's fruit has a source, and the LORD names Himself as it. I'd frame that on my bakery wall, friends.

The answer is right. The verse says, "For the ways of the LORD are right, and the righteous walk in them but the rebellious stumble in them." That's the last thing this whole passage leaves you with. The righteous walk and the rebellious stumble, and we heard that word stumbled in the very first verse.
